note: A text report in CyberChef's section layout (Version, Serial number in decimal and hex, Algorithm ID, Validity, Issuer, Subject, Public Key, Certificate Signature, Extensions) with Forge's own wording of the values: dates are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC (CyberChef's day-first layout is ambiguous and is not reproduced), the names are one attribute per line with the names padded as CyberChef does, and every extension value is written as OpenSSL's x509 -text writes it (Basic Constraints, Key Usage, Extended Key Usage, Subject and Issuer Alternative Name, Subject and Authority Key Identifier, CRL Distribution Points, Authority and Subject Information Access, Certificate Policies, Name Constraints, Policy Mappings and Constraints, Inhibit Any Policy, TLS Feature, Netscape Cert Type), one name per line; any other extension, and a known one whose value is damaged, is shown as hex (the second with the reason). Public keys: RSA (size, modulus, exponent), EC (curve, size, point), DSA (p, q, g, y), EdDSA and X25519/X448 (key); ECDSA and DSA signatures show r and s, RSASSA-PSS shows its hash, mask and salt length. input-format is pem (default), der-hex, base64 or raw (CyberChef's Input format, with the same four choices). Stricter than CyberChef: one certificate (several are Parse X.509 certificate bundles), bytes after it, a cut-short or malformed structure are E_COERCE, and an INTEGER over 65,536 bits is E_LIMIT_VALUE. A multi-valued RDN is shown as separate lines. Compared by running CyberChef 11.5.0: section order, labels and padding are the same, including the Fingerprints section (MD5, SHA1, SHA256 of the DER, lower case without colons; checked with openssl x509 -fingerprint). Differences that stay: dates are YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC where CyberChef writes dd/mm/yyyy hh:mm:ss next to a (dd-mm-yyyy hh:mm:ss) label and the raw time string (ambiguous, so not reproduced); algorithms and curves are named as OpenSSL does (sha256WithRSAEncryption, prime256v1) where jsrsasign says SHA256withRSA and secp256r1; extensions are written as openssl x509 -text does, CyberChef in jsrsasign's style (subjectKeyIdentifier :); CyberChef's ECDSA s value is read from a fixed offset and is wrong when r is not 32 bytes, Forge's is right.

Every certificate of a PEM bundle (or of DER certificates one after the other in der-hex, base64 or raw), each reported as Parse X.509 certificate does under a heading Certificate N of M, separated by a blank line. A malformed certificate is E_COERCE with its number in the message. PEM blocks of other kinds are skipped.

A text report in the layout of CyberChef's Parse X.509 CRL (the shape of openssl crl -text, compared by running it): Certificate Revocation List (CRL): with Version (2 (0x1)), Signature Algorithm, Issuer (names padded as in the certificate report), Last Update and Next Update as RFC 1123 text (Wed, 11 Nov 2026 22:55:51 GMT, as CyberChef; not ambiguous), CRL extensions, Revoked Certificates (Serial Number in upper-case hex, Revocation Date, CRL entry extensions such as the reason code) and the Signature Value in lines of 18 octets. input-format is pem, der-hex, base64 or raw (CyberChef 11.5.0 has the same four and no output-format choice). Differences that stay: CyberChef indents some lines with a tab, Forge uses spaces; the algorithm is named as OpenSSL does; every extension is written as OpenSSL writes it where CyberChef supports four kinds and prints 'Unsupported CRL extension' for the others, and its CRL Number is hex (02) where Forge, like OpenSSL, prints decimal; no revoked certificates is 'No Revoked Certificates.'; stricter: one CRL, bytes after it or a malformed structure are E_COERCE. The dates, serials and signatures were compared with openssl crl -text.

A text report of the PKCS #10 request: Version, Subject, Public Key, Signature, the Attributes (challengePassword, unstructuredName, ...) and the Requested Extensions of the extensionRequest attribute, written like the certificate extensions. input-format is pem (default), der-hex, base64 or raw. The self-signature is not verified (neither does CyberChef's). Compared by running CyberChef: same sections; CyberChef has no Version line and writes the RSA modulus with a leading 00.

The SubjectPublicKeyInfo of each certificate as a PUBLIC KEY PEM block, copied byte for byte (the same as openssl x509 -pubkey), for any key algorithm. input-format is pem (default), der-hex, base64 or raw; the blocks of several certificates follow one another.

A text report of an OpenSSH public key (a .pub, authorized_keys or known_hosts line, the Base64 of the key blob, or its hex; input-format auto, base64 or hex). It starts with CyberChef's lines, in its layout (read from the source; CyberChef's module was not run on SSH keys): Key type: ssh-rsa, Exponent: 0x010001, Modulus: 0x00... (the hex of the fields as they are in the blob, mpint with its leading 00); ssh-dss p:, q:, g:, y:; ecdsa-sha2-* Curve: nistp256 and Point: 0x04...; ssh-ed25519 x: 0x.... Forge adds Length (bits), Comment and the fingerprints as ssh-keygen -l writes them (MD5:aa:bb:..., SHA256:<Base64>), and also reads ssh-ed448 (x:) and the FIDO sk-ssh-ed25519@openssh.com and sk-ecdsa-sha2-nistp256@openssh.com keys (with Application:), which CyberChef prints as unsupported. Stricter than CyberChef: certificate types, a blob cut short or with bytes after the fields, a curve that does not match the type and more than one key are E_COERCE. The report was compared with a Python parse of the blob and hashlib fingerprints.

PEM keys to RFC 7517 JSON Web Keys: PUBLIC KEY, PRIVATE KEY (PKCS #8), RSA PRIVATE KEY, RSA PUBLIC KEY, EC PRIVATE KEY (SEC 1) and the key of a CERTIFICATE; RSA, EC (P-256, P-384, P-521, secp256k1) and OKP (Ed25519, X25519, Ed448, X448, RFC 8037) keys, private keys with their public part (derived with @noble/curves when the file does not carry it). As in CyberChef 11.5.0 (module run) each key is one line of compact JSON and several keys are several lines, with the members in the order of RFC 7518 (kty, n, e, d, p, q, dp, dq, qi; kty, crv, x, y, d); the parameter set-kid ('Set key ID (kid) to RFC 7638 thumbprint') adds kid, the thumbprint of the required members (checked with the key and thumbprint of RFC 7638 section 3.1). Added parameter indent (default 0). Encrypted keys, compressed EC points, multi-prime RSA keys and other algorithms are E_COERCE; CyberChef refuses DSA and RSA PUBLIC KEY and reads certificates the same way.

A JWK, a JWK Set or an array of JWKs to PEM: a public key as PUBLIC KEY (SubjectPublicKeyInfo), a key with d as PRIVATE KEY (PKCS #8), for RSA, EC and OKP keys as in PEM to JWK. The DER written is the same as openssl's (compared byte for byte). EC points are checked to lie on the curve, d is checked to belong to x and y, coordinates must have the full size of the curve, and an RSA private key needs p, q, dp, dq and qi; the symmetric kty oct has no PEM form. All of these are E_COERCE.
